mechanism: Decreases hepatic glucose production and increases insulin sensitivity
side_effects_and_warnings: GI upset (diarrhea, nausea); rare lactic acidosis, especially with renal impairment
pregnancy_lactation: Category B; considered compatible with breastfeeding

mechanism: Inhibits bacterial cell wall synthesis by binding penicillin-binding proteins
common_dosing: 250-500 mg PO every 8 hours, or 875 mg every 12 hours
side_effects_and_warnings: Diarrhea, rash; hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis in penicillin-allergic patients
pregnancy_lactation: Considered safe in pregnancy and breastfeeding

mechanism: Inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme, reducing angiotensin II and aldosterone
side_effects_and_warnings: Dry cough, hyperkalemia, angioedema (rare but serious)
pregnancy_lactation: Contraindicated in pregnancy (fetotoxic); use caution in breastfeeding

mechanism: Thought to inhibit central prostaglandin synthesis; exact mechanism unclear
common_dosing: 325-1000 mg PO every 4-6 hours, max 3-4 g/day
side_effects_and_warnings: Hepatotoxicity in overdose; generally well tolerated at therapeutic doses
pregnancy_lactation: Considered safe in pregnancy and breastfeeding at recommended doses
